findings.label: High Contrast ring read after mouse clicks
findings.location: .kiro/skills/heuristic-ux-audit/references/evidence-capture.md:131-141 (template High Contrast block), :76-80 (popover-trigger adaptation), :226-243 (§ Interaction states focus and High Contrast bullets); apps/web/src/w360/w360.css:5061; apps/web/src/w360/ui.tsx:936, :1045
findings.issue: The template switches to High Contrast with two mouse clicks (W360's Menu then refocuses its trigger from script) and only then calls field.focus(). After a pointer click, Chromium matches :focus-visible on a scripted focus only for text inputs, and every W360 outline ring, including the High Contrast !important one, is a :focus-visible rule. In the pinned Chromium a scripted focus on a button after two clicks gave :focus-visible false and outline none; a text input, or a button after a Shift press or a keyboard-driven menu, gave true. So the High Contrast ring of any popover trigger, chip or list row (the eval's + Filter trigger included) records as none, which pass 12 treats as a finding against design.md § Microinteractions stance, and any non-text ring read after a click (an option in a popover opened by click) has the same problem in Dark.
findings.action: In the template, press a key (await page.keyboard.press('Shift')) or drive the theme menu from the keyboard before field.focus(), and add to the § Interaction states focus bullet that any ring on a control that is not a text input, read after a click, needs a key press first.
